strengths: Significance: Repeatedly solving MIPs with shared structure is a useful application. PreMIO incorporates learned predictions through simple linear constraints, making integration with commercial solvers straightforward.

Methodological merit: The four complementary regions in Algorithm 1 preserve global optimality when all are solved completely. Cardinality budgets also provide more flexibility than fixing individual predicted variables.
Empirical merits: Figure 1 reports promising time-to-target improvements across knapsack, set covering, and unit commitment, using both Gurobi and COPT under several heuristic settings.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The overall pipeline is understandable. Remark 6 and Section 4.4 explicitly acknowledge imperfect probability estimates, infeasible restricted problems, and parameter sensitivity. No material research-ethics concerns are apparent from the reported public and synthetic datasets.
weaknesses: Soundness of the probability guarantees: Appendix B.1, Equation (4), incorrectly factorizes an expectation over the shared test instance. Independent training datasets do not imply independent prediction errors. Separately, Theorem 2 treats the prediction-selected sets U and L as fixed while using unconditional accuracy bounds. High overall accuracy can coexist with systematically incorrect positive predictions, so A3 does not justify this concentration argument. These are substantive gaps in the central theoretical contribution.

Connection between theory and implementation: Theorem 3 assumes exact conditional means and independence of optimal coordinates. Neither is established for logistic regressions trained on shared, constraint-coupled MIP instances. There are no held-out calibration or coverage measurements connecting these assumptions to practice, and larger SCP training instances use a 10% optimality-gap tolerance. The acknowledged idealizations therefore leave the implemented method's claimed optimal-solution retention unsupported.

Pruning justification: Section 3.2 claims the complementary branches become infeasible when the preferred region excludes every global optimum. In that situation, at least one complementary branch contains a better feasible solution satisfying the added objective cutoff. Even when the preferred region contains an optimum, cheap certification through LP relaxations is not generally guaranteed.

Evaluation: The reported MIPLIB improvement concerns an outcome-selected 57 of 132 instances, excluding infeasible restricted problems and joint timeouts. Full-set results with fallback costs are needed to establish overall benefit. Section 4.2 measures time to PreMIO's own attained objective without reporting matched-budget solution gaps or clear timeout handling. Statistical uncertainty is also absent, with only five SCUC test instances per configuration.

Originality: The method is closely related to prediction-based neighborhoods in reference [11] and local branching in [12]. Comparisons against variable fixing, learned diving, and local branching using the same predictor are missing. Ablations of the separate cardinality budgets and concentration-derived thresholds are needed to establish what the proposed contribution adds.

Reproducibility: Solver versions, logistic-regression training details, and a code link are not provided. The MKP capacity formula contains a 1/n factor that, as written, makes nonzero feasible solutions overwhelmingly unlikely at the stated dimensions, requiring clarification against the reported difficult solves. Table 3 does not document all 57 retained instances and duplicates blp-ar98.

Presentation and parameter specification: Appendix D defines misclassification fractions as 'accuracy' and proposes maximizing them. It then recommends tau approximately 0.1 despite specifying tau in [0.5, 1). These inconsistencies directly affect implementation of the claimed hyperparameter-selection procedure.
